subject: DPA amendment: dataflow, retention, and 'no-train' operational workstream
messages:
From: Claire Johnson <claire.j@healthsprint.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA amendment: dataflow, retention, and 'no-train' asks

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the call last week. As we move toward a pilot with Redwood we need a short DPA amendment focused on three items before we can sign:

1) A clear no-training / no-model-improvement commitment for customer interactions (and a short definition for what counts as "training").
2) Operational evidence that data stays within US regions (KMS residency or onshore encryption keys) for production traffic and any SFTP export paths.
3) A subprocessors appendix and a retention timeline for interaction logs and derived artifacts (we need a 90-day default retention and an option to shorten to 30 days).

Attached is our suggested redline to the DPA — we called this out inline (HealthSprint_DPA_redline_v3.docx). Two quick clarifications we need up front:
- Prompt/response ownership: we want an explicit confirmation that interactive prompts and model responses are the customer's output and are not used to build or improve Redwood models.
- Export/escrow: we want a plan for transferring logs/derivatives to our SFTP (we provided onboarding details in a separate checklist).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Commit contractually to a non-training promise for HealthSprint traffic?
- Provide KMS-onshore routing or attest to key separation?
- Share a current subprocessors list and your typical update cadence?

We'd like to aim to finalize the amendment and evidence pack within two weeks so procurement can approve the pilot budget.

Best,
Claire Johnson
Lead Counsel, Compliance & Privacy
HealthSprint

--
Attachment: HealthSprint_DPA_redline_v3.docx (docx, 42 KB)
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: Claire Johnson <claire.j@healthsprint.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA amendment: dataflow, retention, and 'no-train' asks

Hi Claire — thanks for the redline and the clear list. Looping in David (Privacy Ops) and Kimberly (Security) so we can get operational answers and the subprocessors snapshot. Quick summary from our side and proposed next steps: 

Summary answers (high level):
- Contractual no-training commitment: yes, Redwood can agree to a contractual prohibition on using HealthSprint production interaction data to improve our public models. We will provide explicit language. We need to confirm scope: 
  * Does this apply to all traffic including logs/derivatives and ephemeral KV cache?
- KMS/residency: we support per-customer key routing for hosted instances and can provide onshore KMS or customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private modes. For hosted pilots we can attest to an onshore KMS binding and provide a short attestation.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a subprocessors list and an automated notification cadence (30-days for major changes). We'll attach the current list and a brief dataflow diagram.

Operational evidence we can provide within 7 business days:
- Signed attestation and sample config showing KMS onshore routing (pdf).
- Subprocessors inventory (csv) + last-30-day access audit extract (redacted).
- SFTP onboarding checklist and one-time export run plan (we can do an initial SFTP push to your staging host).
- Retention controls: we can set tenant-level retention TTLs (default 90 days, configurable down to 0 days).

Open items:
- Precise definition of "training": our proposed clause will ban using your interaction logs to update weights, fine-tune, or include in training corpora for any Redwood models (including internal research). That still allows ephemeral caching and routing optimizations for latency control; if you want to prohibit KV cache reuse across tenants we can add that.
- Prompt/response IP: our standard approach is that prompts and generated outputs are customer data and we will not claim ownership; we will add explicit language matching your request.

Attachments I am including: dataflow-diagram.png (ops diagram) and SFTP_onboarding_checklist.pdf.

Proposed next step: legal + ops sync (30 minutes) Thursday 12:00pm PT to walk through your redlines and finalize definitions. If that works I'll send a calendar invite. After the call we will post a short evidence pack to the Drive link and upload the attestation to DocuSign for signature.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Legal (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: dataflow-diagram.png, SFTP_onboarding_checklist.pdf
From: Claire Johnson <claire.j@healthsprint.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.p@healthsprint.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA amendment: dataflow, retention, and 'no-train' asks

Thanks Lauren — Thursday works. I've reviewed your summary and added two small redlines in the doc where we want further specificity:

1) Narrower definition of "improvement": we ask that "improvement" include any derivation used for model training, evaluation, or benchmark datasets (not just weight updates).
2) Subprocessor change notification: we want a 15-day notification period for any subprocessors that handle interactive data or logs.

I've attached an updated redline with inline comments (HealthSprint_DPA_redline_v3.docx). Operationally Raj (our platform lead) added the following asks:
- Can Redwood perform the first SFTP export into our staging SFTP by Aug 2?
- We'd prefer the initial attestation to include a sample audit log (redacted) showing KMS key usage for a recent export.

If you can confirm those two items on the Thursday call, Procurement will try to get the PO approved for a limited pilot.

Claire
Claire Johnson
Lead Counsel, Compliance & Privacy
HealthSprint

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA amendment: dataflow, retention, and 'no-train' asks

Claire — great, thanks for the clarifications and Raj's asks. Confirming outcomes and action items from our side before Thursday's sync (I sent the calendar invite for Thu 12:00pm PT):

Confirmed commitments:
- No-training clause: Redwood will add explicit contractual language prohibiting use of HealthSprint production interactions, logs, or derivatives for model training, evaluation corpora, benchmarking datasets, or research that would surface HealthSprint content. We will include a definition in the DPA that captures weight updates, fine-tuning, and inclusion in training/eval corpora.
- Prompt/response IP: we'll add language that generated outputs and prompts are Customer Data and Redwood assigns no ownership to them.
- Subprocessor notice: we can accept a 15-day notice for subprocessors that process interactive traffic; we will provide the current inventory and our process for emergency changes.
- Retention: default 90 days with tenant-configurable TTL; we will confirm the mechanism for a customer-triggered shorter retention (30 days) in the evidence pack.

Operational deliverables we will provide by the call or within 3 business days after the call:
- Onshore KMS attestation PDF + a redacted sample audit snippet showing key usage for an SFTP export.
- Subprocessors inventory CSV and our last 30-day access audit (redacted).
- A dry-run SFTP export plan: we can schedule the first staging push by Aug 2; ops will need a staging SFTP host + credentials from Raj.
- Updated DPA redline incorporating the agreed language. We'll upload these to the Drive link and put the DocuSign envelope live once we close the definitions.

Action items:
- Raj: please send the staging SFTP hostname and a test account before Tue Jul 27 so Ops can schedule the push.
- David/Kimberly: prepare attestation + audit snippet and the subprocessors CSV (I'll track in the evidence folder).
- Claire: confirm that the proposed definition of "improvement" in the redline matches your expectations or point to a short alternative sentence before the call.

I'll follow up after the call with the evidence pack link and the updated redline. Thanks — we look forward to getting the pilot started.

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Legal (Contracts)
Redwood Inference
